subject.title: Feature: agent-controlled model profiles and task-aware model switching from Telegram

question: Should OpenClaw limit this issue to alias-first multi-model onboarding, or establish a new profile contract that also owns auth, fallback, parameters, cost policy, and automatic task routing?
rationale: Current main already supplies the secure user/agent session-switching mechanism, but the remaining alternatives have substantially different configuration, compatibility, authorization, and product consequences that cannot be selected from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Alias-first onboarding
options.body: Extend onboarding or the model configuration wizard to add several allowed aliased models while reusing the existing picker, commands, status, and `session_status` mutation path.

options.title: Full profile contract
options.body: Design a new first-class schema for bundled model, auth, fallback, parameter, cost, and routing policy with explicit upgrade and authorization rules before implementation.

options.title: Keep advanced configuration
options.body: Retain the existing alias and session-switching features as manually configured advanced behavior and decline additional onboarding or automatic routing for now.

recommendation.title: Alias-first onboarding
recommendation.body: Extend onboarding or the model configuration wizard to add several allowed aliased models while reusing the existing picker, commands, status, and `session_status` mutation path.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged session-pin and fallback work spans the shared runtime and Telegram behavior central to choosing this boundary.
